candidates.label: Cathedral European Beech R2
candidates.prompt: Botanically accurate mature European beech in full summer leaf, photogrammetry-quality game tree. Tall smooth trunk and low sweeping scaffold limbs stay visible inside a broad oval crown. Build the crown from hundreds of thin flat separate leaf sprays, each smaller than a human torso, with branching and sky between them. No continuous sculpted foliage masses, foam, broccoli, spheres, or topiary shell. Restrained roots. Complete isolated tree, no ground, vines, moss, props, text, or background.
candidates.texturePrompt: Photorealistic healthy midsummer European beech. Smooth dry silver-gray bark with faint warm brown seams on trunk and every branch, never green, mossy, wet, or washed out. Leaves alone vary from deep forest-green interiors through rich natural green to restrained fresh-green tips. Neutral unlit albedo, detailed bark and leaf normals, nonmetallic, high roughness, zero emission or baked light. Preserve bark and foliage as visually distinct surfaces.

rejectedPreviews.reason: Species read survived, but dense cone-like crown and fused foam clusters failed the fine-leaf gate.
Fluted trunk read survived, but the canopy was a dense vertical shell of oversized clumps.
Fused solid foliage curtains hid the branch hierarchy and failed the open-twig contract.
Strong scaffold silhouette, but foliage resolved as oversized cotton-ball masses.
Second attempt retained solid curtain strips and theatrical exposed roots; replaced with black willow.
Third willow attempt again collapsed into solid weeping curtains; replaced by related riparian cottonwood.
Cottonwood was interpreted as hanging cotton tassels on a mostly dead crown; failed lush-summer requirement.
